newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks switch to losses at close.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks switch to losses at close.

text.p: Argentine stocks surrendered gains and closed lower Wednesday on the back of a turnaround on Wall Street, dealers said.

"The markets are behaving in an erratic fashion and locally the bolsa is having trouble setting new highs," said Humberto Lopez at traders Wainbuch. "It looks tired, overextended, and needs some time to regroup."
The blue-chip MerVal index shed 0.6 percent to close at 820.14, slipping off a peak of 830.16 which had set a new five-year high.

"I think we can blame this volatile spell on next week's meeting of the U.S. Federal Reserve," another trader said. "People were too confident there wouldn't be a rate hike, so the markets kept rallying. But then last minute they start to wonder...what if we were wrong?"
"It's a classic case of nervous reshuffling," he added.
The broad market index closed off 0.4 percent, with losers edging out winners 31 to 29 and 20 stocks closing flat.
Floor volume picked up to 40.8 million pesos from 34.1 million pesos, while over-the-counter turnover swelled to 101.9 million pesos from 82.8 million Tuesday.
The top main-tier gainers was pulp and paper maker Celulosa, which jumped 3.8 percent, continuing its rollercoaster ride after a spate of buyout rumors.
Steelmaker Siderca tacked on 1.1 percent and real estate developer Irsa climbed 0.7 percent.
Among MerVal losers carmakers Sevel and Ciadea tumbled 7.1 percent and 2.9 percent, respectively, while steelmaker Siderar shed 2.3 percent.
